context.why: The package's promise has two halves. The first — install a backend and its pages appear — was built in the previous story. This story holds the second: a backend you have NOT installed contributes nothing at all, and costs your project none of that backend's dependencies. That is what makes the first half safe to rely on, because a package that contributes pages for an absent backend puts a broken link in front of a person, and a package that installs a backend to be sure hands every project that backend's own constraints.
context.environment: Poetry project. Run everything with 'poetry run ...' from the worktree root. Tests: 'poetry run pytest'. The full verify command is '/home/sam/.openclaw/workspaces/forge/engineering-org/kit/forge verify --repo .' — run it once, at your report. The test settings inherit from demo/settings.py, which installs the backend; this story needs a settings module that does not.
spec_sections: User Story 2 - A backend you have not installed costs you nothing
prior_decisions: D1 — every surface reads mvp_payments.namespaces.available_contributions() rather than asking apps.is_installed for itself. If this story finds a surface that asks for itself, the fix is to route it through that function, not to special-case the surface.
D3 — availability is two questions. is_available() asks the application registry; is_reachable() additionally asks whether the pages reverse. An absent backend fails the first, so it fails both.
context.conventions: CONSTITUTION.md Articles X (test structure: mirror the source tree, group into Test<Subject> classes) and XVI (assert rendered output, never the presence of a class name).

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the project's test settings, when a variant is built with the backend removed from the installed applications, then the suite can run against it and Django starts cleanly.

Given the backend is not installed, when a signed-in person opens the Account Center, then no navigation entry and no card belonging to that backend appear in the rendered page, and none of its page addresses resolve. Assert against what is rendered, not against the menu objects.

Given the package's own source, when its declared runtime dependencies are read, then they are exactly django and django-mvp; and when every module under mvp_payments/ is scanned, then none imports a payment backend or a payment provider's library. Confirm the existing assertions in tests/test_app.py actually reach the modules the previous story added — mvp_payments/namespaces/ and anything else new — rather than assuming they do.

Given the tests above, when they are run, then they pass without any production change; if one does not, the fix routes the offending surface through available_contributions() rather than special-casing it.
